prompt_text: Who is the best roofer in Denver for hail damage repair?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” roofer for hail damage in Denver — the right contractor depends on your location, the extent of damage, your insurance situation, and what you value (price, speed, workmanship warranty, insurance-claim help). I can’t browse current local listings from here, but I can help you find the best contractor for your situation. Quick advice and next steps:

How to pick the best roofer for hail damage
- Check credentials: contractor license (if required locally), business insurance (liability + workers’ comp), and local trade association membership.
- Look for manufacturer certifications such as GAF Master Elite, CertainTeed SELECT Shingle Master, etc. These indicate training and access to better warranties.
- Experience with hail claims: choose companies that regularly handle insurance claims and can provide documentation/photos for adjusters (but avoid roof “storm-chasers” who pressure homeowners after storms).
- Reviews & reputation: read Google/Yelp/BBB reviews, ask for recent references in Denver neighborhoods, and check how long they’ve been in business locally.
- Written, detailed estimates: scope of work, materials (brand/type/color), removal & disposal, permit responsibility, start/completion dates, clean-up and tarp policy, and specific warranties (manufacturer + workmanship).
- Get at least 2–3 competitive written estimates. Compare like-for-like materials and warranties.
- Permits & inspections: confirm they’ll pull permits and handle municipal inspections.
- Payment terms: avoid large upfront payments (25–50% deposit is common), and never pay the full cost until work is complete and you’re satisfied.

Where to look
- Search for “GAF Master Elite roofer Denver” or “CertainTeed SELECT Denver”
- Check Google Maps, Yelp, Angie’s List/Angi, HomeAdvisor, and the BBB for ratings and complaints
- Local restoration franchises (e.g., Paul Davis or ServiceMaster Restore) often handle hail/insurance claims
- Colorado Roofing Contractors Association or Denver-area trade groups for member lists

Questions to ask a roofer when they inspect
- Do you provide a written roof inspection report with photos?
- Are you licensed and insured? Can you provide proof?
- Are you certified by any shingle manufacturers?
- Will you assist with the insurance claim and meet the adjuster?
- What warranties do you offer (materials and workmanship)? Are they transferable?
- Do you pull permits and who inspects the work?
- What is the project timeline, payment schedule, and cleanup plan?

If you want, I can:
- Help you draft a short questionnaire to send to contractors.
- Review and compare 2–3 written estimates if you paste them here.
- Suggest specific Denver contractors if you tell me your ZIP code or neighborhood and allow me to search (note: I can’t browse from here, but I can tell you how to find top-rated local firms).
